generation.final_prompt:
Rendering style:
Create an authored editorial illustration for a serious technology newspaper.

Direction:
- authored editorial print language
- deliberate simplified shapes with clear focal hierarchy
- restrained limited palette
- subtle physical print texture
- controlled abstraction and strong negative space
- non-photorealistic but factually grounded representation
- newspaper and social-card readability

Fixed factual and safety restrictions:
- Do not render visible text, captions, headlines, or newspaper typography.
- Do not render logos or trademarks.
- Do not fabricate visible factual evidence.
- Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
- Do not imitate a named or living artist.

Profile-specific exclusions:
- glossy CGI
- luxury product render
- generic futuristic concept art
- cyberpunk or neon
- glowing circuit-board decoration
- floating particles
- heroic centered hardware
- server rack treated as monument or skyscraper
- generic server room
- advertising composition
- airbrushed gradients
- synthetic chrome
- excessive pseudo-technical detail
- malformed or visible text
- labels
- diagrams with words

Exact source facts:
Title: APPLE IS WORKING ON AI AGENT FOR DEVICE CONTROL, APPS, BROWSING AND CODING
Summary: Apple is developing an autonomous AI agent that can get things done on behalf of users similar to offerings by OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and others. The company is currently seeking a senior engineering manager for a proactive, agentic AI assistant that can write code, browse the web, control apps, and navigate devices on a user's behalf. Apple is working on agents that can plan and carry out multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs while coordinating specialized subagents along the way. The company's App Store has been dominated by AI agents, so it has introduced a new warning in the upcoming macOS 27.3 update that prompts users to reconsider granting third-party agents permission to control their Macs.

Editorial idea:
The promise of an autonomous assistant is expanding at the same time that users are being warned to scrutinize the permissions such agents require.

Central subject:
An autonomous software agent acting across apps, browsers, command lines, code, APIs, and devices on a user's behalf.

Visual relationship:
A capable delegated agent approaches a series of user-controlled access points, conveying the tension between convenience and permission without depicting the agent as fully independent of human approval.

Composition:
A human hand remains on one side of a partially open doorway while a distinct abstract assistant presence reaches toward several connected openings beyond it. The human side is clearly the point of authorization; the assistant's path stops short of unrestricted passage.

Permitted literal elements:
human hand
partially open doorway
abstract assistant presence
multiple app-like openings
visible boundary between authorization and action

Abstraction level:
medium

Story-specific forbidden elements:
racks
chips
laptops
robots
clouds
shields
arrows
charts
skyscrapers
chess
handshakes
split-screen conflict
logos
rendered text
generic glowing circuitry

Likely failure modes to avoid:
Depicting the agent as a humanoid robot rather than software
Showing unrestricted autonomous control without the user's permission boundary
Using generic futuristic interface decoration instead of the documented app and device access
Making the warning feel like a separate security story rather than a constraint on the agent's use

Global factual restrictions:
Do not fabricate visible factual evidence. Do not imitate a named or living artist. Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
Do not render any words, letters, numbers, labels, captions, annotations, signage, diagrams with text, logos, watermarks, or pseudo-writing anywhere in the image.
If the concept cannot be represented without visible text, represent the relationship through shape, scale, spacing, direction, grouping, interruption, containment, or contrast instead.
